headline: Loss narrows as acquisition-driven revenue surges
summary_short: Intuitive Machines reported a Q2 FY2026 per-share loss of $0.16, narrowing 35.9% q/q and 27.1% y/y, as revenue jumped to $206.2 million from $50.3 million a year earlier on the Lanteris acquisition.
summary_long: Total revenue rose to $206.2 million from $50.3 million a year ago, mainly from the January 2026 Lanteris acquisition ($166.7 million contributed). Legacy lunar-mission revenue was roughly flat, with IM-3 and IM-6 gains offset by an IM-4 cost-estimate charge and a NASA Near Space Network schedule delay. Cost of revenue rose $108.1 million, mostly Lanteris-related. G&A rose $44.8 million on higher compensation, stock-based pay, and professional-services costs. Backlog reached $1.76 billion, up $1.55 billion, including $612.8 million of acquired Lanteris backlog and a new multi-satellite award.
confidence_notes: Shard EPS (Yahoo-sourced, -$0.1603) is on a different basis than the 10-Q's GAAP net loss per Class A share (-$0.29 for the quarter, after preferred dividends and noncontrolling-interest allocations); using the shard's ledger-sourced value per KPI discipline and flagging the divergence here.

drivers.explanation: Loss narrowed as Lanteris-driven revenue ($166.7M) outpaced the $108.1M rise in cost of revenue and $44.8M G&A increase.

Revenue growth came almost entirely from the Lanteris acquisition; legacy lunar-mission revenue was roughly flat as IM-3/IM-6 gains offset an IM-4 cost-estimate charge and a NASA Near Space Network delay.
